items.headline: Jarry stopped 31 of 34 shots in Tuesday's 4-3 shootout loss to the Devils.
items.text: Jarry had posted consecutive shutouts in his last two starts. He kept the Devils off the board in the first period, but they cashed in three times in the second and Arseny Gritsyuk had the decisive tally in the shootout. Despite the setback, Jarry has taken big strides over the last week-plus to prove he can handle the starting job while Devon Levi (undisclosed) is out. Jarry is 4-1-3 with a 2.57 GAA and an .898 save percentage across eight starts this season. The Oilers are back home for their next game, hosting the Ducks on Thursday.

items.headline: Jarry will guard the road crease in Tuesday's clash against New Jersey, per Mike Morreale of NHL.com.
items.text: Jarry has been heating up, as he's avoided a regulation loss in each of his three outings since Oct. 24. Overall, the 31-year-old netminder has a 4-1-2 record, a 2.54 GAA, two shutouts and an .895 save percentage across seven appearances this season. With Devon Levi (undisclosed) still sidelined, Jarry remains a solid option in deep fantasy formats given his recent success and the offense skating in front of him. He'll face a relatively-tough test Tuesday against New Jersey, who currently rank 10th in the NHL with 3.43 goals per game this season.

items.headline: Jarry stopped all 18 shots on net he saw in Saturday's 4-0 shutout win over the Islanders.
items.text: After an up and down start to the 2026-27 campaign, Jarry has stepped up his game as of late, earning his second consecutive win and first shutout of the season in Saturday's game. Overall, the 31-year-old backstop is up to a 4-1-2 record, a 2.53 GAA and a .901 save percentage across seven outings this season. With Devon Levi (undisclosed) on injured reserve and Frederik Andersen (knee) still on the injured non-roster list, Jarry should continue to command the opportunities between the pipes for Edmonton, raising his fantasy value until Levi is set to return. Jarry is unbeaten in regulation over his last three outings, making him a solid streaming option in most leagues for the time being.

items.headline: Jarry is expected to start on the road against the Islanders on Saturday, per Stephen Whyno of the Associated Press.
items.text: Jarry is coming off a 24-save shutout victory over Calgary on Wednesday. He has a 3-1-2 record, 2.95 GAA and .882 save percentage in six appearances with Edmonton in 2026-27. The Islanders are 4-1-1 while averaging 3.17 goals per game across their past six games.

Instead, the team hopes that the 38-year-old will be able to take part in Tuesday's morning skate in Columbus since the Panthers aren't slated to have many opportunities to practice in November. Head coach Paul Maurice said last week that Marchand was approximately three weeks away from returning, so it seems as though he could be in consideration for game action as soon as mid-November.

injuries.longComment: Barkov isn't expected to return to game action during the road trip, which begins Saturday in Washington and concludes Tuesday in Columbus, but the Panthers aren't slated to have many practices in November, so the 31-year-old could join the team for morning skate prior to Florida's game against the Blue Jackets. Maurice said last week that Barkov was still believed to be approximately four weeks away from returning to game action, so it seems unlikely that he'll be in the mix to return until at least mid-to-late November.

injuries.longComment: Ristolainen's placement on injured reserve was expected after head coach Rick Tocchet announced that the 32-year-old blueliner would miss roughly two weeks. Ristolainen had already missed nine games due to the same hand issue earlier in the season, but the injury flared back up in Saturday's clash against the Ducks. When healthy, he's been solid with a goal, five shots on net, seven hits and seven blocked shots across four appearances this season. In his absence, Cam York has been activated off injured reserve and should take on some of the minutes vacated by Ristolainen.
injuries.shortComment: Ristolainen (hand) was placed on injured reserve, retroactive to Oct. 24, on Tuesday.

injuries.longComment: Grebenkin's upper-body injury has been revealed to be an issue with his back, which he has successfully had repaired. The 23-year-old winger is expected to miss the majority of the 2026-27 campaign, but his current timeline for return, barring any setbacks, projects him back sometime after the All-Star break in mid-February. When he does return, Grebenkin will look to build off a positive rookie campaign, where he compiled four goals, 14 points, 32 shots on net, 86 hits and 17 blocked shots across 55 regular-season outings in 2025-26.
injuries.shortComment: Grebenkin (back) underwent successful surgery and is expected to miss at least four months.

items.headline: Douglas (upper body) is listed as day-to-day and is expected to miss Tuesday's practice.
items.text: Douglas has been kept in check offensively across four appearances this season, as he's logged zero points, seven PIM, one shot on goal, 10 hits and five blocked shots. With the 26-year-old forward slated to miss Tuesday's practice, his status for Wednesday's home clash against the Kraken is up in the air. If he's to miss the contest, Jani Nyman would be his likely replacement.

items.headline: Douglas had seven PIM in Friday's 6-2 loss to the Flames.
items.text: Douglas and Adam Klapka had a heavyweight tilt in this contest, though Douglas was a little overzealous with his punches and got an extra penalty. That led to a goal for the Flames, which could be bad news for Douglas sticking in the lineup for the rematch Wednesday in Seattle. The 26-year-old enforcer has played in four games this season, logging 10 hits, five blocked shots and one shot on goal in addition to his PIM count from Friday. Jani Nyman was the extra forward Friday but would be a much more natural replacement as the Kraken navigate life without Jared McCann (lower body) for the rest of the calendar year.

injuries.longComment: McCann had one goal in five games before sitting out Saturday's 5-1 loss to Minnesota. He has earned five assists, eight points, 28 shots on net, three blocked shots and six hits in 11 appearances this season. With McCann unavailable, Kaapo Kakko moved up to the top line in Saturday's game.
injuries.shortComment: McCann (lower body) will be out for approximately 10 weeks, the team announced Sunday.

injuries.longComment: The Kraken said that there would be a "gradual progression to return to hockey," so Melanson shouldn't be expected to play for a while. The 23-year-old suffered the injury in Seattle's Season Opener against Calgary on Oct. 1. Melanson had two goals and five points in 36 regular-season outings with the Kraken in 2025-26.
injuries.shortComment: Melanson's upper-body injury was diagnosed Saturday as an anterior mediastinum hematoma with vascular pseudo aneurysm. He will continue to be evaluated and is out indefinitely.

injuries.longComment: Lindgren suffered the upper-body injury in the first period of Tuesday's clash against the Golden Knights before he ultimately was removed from the game ahead of the second stanza. Prior to going down, the 28-year-old blueliner compiled a plus-three rating, seven PIM, three shots on goal and four blocked shots across four outings to begin the 2026-27 campaign. While he is sidelined over the next four to six weeks, Josh Mahura is expected to see an increased role.
injuries.shortComment: Lindgren (upper body) was placed on injured reserve by the Kraken on Thursday and is expected to miss four to six weeks.

injuries.longComment: O'Brien was initially announced on injured reserve Sunday, but his status has since been clarified. He is considered week-to-week at this time. The Kraken have a few options for when he gets healthy -- as a 19-year-old first-round pick (2025), he is eligible for the AHL if Seattle thinks that would be best for his development.
injuries.shortComment: O'Brien (lower body) was placed on non-roster injured reserve Wednesday.

items.text: Mailloux began his conditioning assignment Monday, and he didn't end up playing in any AHL games. The 23-year-old hasn't been activated off injured reserve, so he might not be ready to return yet. Mailloux might serve on St. Louis' third pairing once he's healthy.

items.headline: The Blues assigned Mailloux (hand) to AHL Springfield for a conditioning assignment Monday.
items.text: Mailloux underwent surgery to address a hand injury in late September, and general manager Alexander Steen said at the time that the 23-year-old defenseman would be re-evaluated in approximately eight weeks. While it's encouraging that Mailloux will join the Blues' minor-league affiliate as part of his recovery process, it's not yet clear when he'll be able to return to game action at the NHL level since he's still several weeks away from when he was initially scheduled to be re-evaluated.

injuries.longComment: Krug's move to long-term injured reserve was partially a financial decision, as it allows the Blues to exceed the salary cap by $4 million. The 35-year-old blueliner hasn't played since the 2023-24 campaign, but he hasn't officially ruled out a return. Regardless of when he decides to hang up his skates, the 13-year NHL veteran will be remembered as an excellent two-way player, as he currently sits at 483 points, 621 hits and 832 blocked shots across 778 regular-season outings.
injuries.shortComment: Krug (ankle) was placed on long-term injured reserve by the Blues on Monday, per PuckPedia.

injuries.longComment: Based on Tucker's timeline, he shouldn't be expected back until mid-November, though it could certainly be longer. With Logan Mailloux (hand) also sidelined long-term, Adam Jiricek could see an extended run on the blue line. For his part, even once cleared to play, Tucker is unlikely to offer much in the way of fantasy value given his limited offensive upside.
injuries.shortComment: Tucker had arthroscopic knee surgery and will be re-assessed in six weeks, the team announced Wednesday.

items.headline: Tavares (lower body) resumed skating Tuesday and is now listed as day-to-day, per David Alter of The Hockey News.
items.text: Tavares took part in his first team skate since going down with a lower-body injury in the Maple Leafs' clash against Buffalo on Oct. 15. The 36-year-old center was wearing a red non-contact sweater at morning skate, indicating that he's not quite ready to return. However, his activation from injured reserve is an indication that his return is near. When healthy this season, the 18-year NHL veteran has two goals, seven points, 17 shots on net and five blocked shots across seven appearances. He'll have shot to return in Saturday's clash against the Canadiens.

injuries.longComment: Less than 24 hours after Merzlikins was traded to the Maple Leafs, a timetable for his return to action has been provided. The 32-year-old backstop had an up and down season in 2025-26, where he posted a 14-11-3 record, a 3.39 GAA and an .883 save percentage across 30 regular-season outings. He won't be rushed into action, as the Leafs new goaltender tandem of Sergei Bobrovsky and Anthony Stolarz are still expected to handle the majority of reps between the pipes this upcoming season. However, when Merzlikins is ready to return, he's the clear No. 3 option in Toronto's organization and could still see some playing time at the NHL level if he isn't sent down to AHL Toronto.
injuries.shortComment: Merzlikins is expected to miss 4-6 months to begin the 2026-27 regular season while recovering from a shoulder injury, per Luke Fox of Sportsnet.
